theme.title: NBA Mix 61
theme.subtitle: Five moments from across NBA history
theme.recap: Five NBA stories, five different numbers: a quick tour of stars, teams, records and surprises.

questions.prompt: The 1998–99 lockout cut the regular season to how many games per team?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Due to a lockout, the regular season began on February 5, 1999, and was cut from 82 games to 50.

funFacts.text: The season began unusually late after the league and players' association settled their labor dispute.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the season, which began on February 5, 1999

funFacts.text: Chicago's championship dynasty disintegrated during the stoppage, with Jordan and Phil Jackson leaving.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Phil Jackson and Michael Jordan temporarily retire

funFacts.text: The New York Knicks reached the Finals from the bottom playoff seed, an extraordinary outcome.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: this was the only NBA Finals to feature an eighth-seeded team

questions.prompt: What did Dennis Rodman average in rebounds in 1991–92, his first rebounding title?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He collected an astounding 18.7 per game, winning his first of seven consecutive rebounding crowns

funFacts.text: Rodman made his first All-NBA team during the season when his rebounding suddenly exploded.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: and making his first All-NBA Team

funFacts.text: Kevin Willis argued Rodman could focus so completely on boards because he had few offensive duties.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Willis lamented that Rodman had an advantage in winning the rebounding title with his lack of offensive responsibilities

funFacts.text: Detroit's bruising identity had already produced back-to-back titles while Rodman was developing as a defender.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Detroit beat Portland in five games and claimed their second title

questions.prompt: In the 2022 title clincher, Golden State went on an unanswered run of how many points?
questions.note: 21–0, the longest in modern Finals history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 21–0 run was the longest such run in modern Finals history.

funFacts.text: Boston opened the deciding game with a quick surge, but Golden State answered before the first quarter ended.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Boston took a 14–2 lead to start the game

funFacts.text: The Warriors' swarming defense forced repeated Boston turnovers before halftime.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors forced 12 turnovers in the first half

funFacts.text: The Warriors were only the second visiting team to clinch an NBA championship on Boston's floor.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: This was the second time that a road team won an NBA championship in Boston

questions.prompt: What was Hedo Türkoğlu's assists-per-game average in 2008–09?
questions.context: Magic · point-forward in a Finals season
questions.note: 4.9 assists per game while running much of Orlando's offense.

funFacts.text: Türkoğlu collected 375 assists across the regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Hedo Türkoğlu | SF | 77 | 77 | 2,815 | 410 | 375

funFacts.text: His late-game heroics helped Orlando survive Philadelphia early in the playoffs.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: highlighted by forward Hedo Türkoğlu's game winner in game four of that series

funFacts.text: After the season, Orlando sent Türkoğlu to Toronto in a multi-team deal.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Following the season, Türkoğlu was traded to the Toronto Raptors

questions.prompt: In Game 2 of the 1999 West finals, San Antonio came back from how many points down to win on Sean Elliott's "Memorial Day Miracle"?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Spurs trailed by 17 points against the Trail Blazers in Game 2

funFacts.text: Sean Elliott hit the decisive long-distance shot to sink Portland in the conference finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a game-winning three-pointer from Elliott, which was dubbed as the "Memorial Day Miracle"

funFacts.text: San Antonio went on to sweep Portland, becoming the first former ABA franchise to reach the NBA Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: becoming the first former ABA team to advance to the NBA Finals

funFacts.text: Before the Portland showdown, San Antonio had swept Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal's Lakers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Lakers, who were led by the All-Star trio of Shaquille O'Neal, Kobe Bryant and Glen Rice
